summary: The code is syntactically valid and imports are fine, but it fails critical implementation and logic requirements: main() does not execute the simulation or produce outputs, and Simulation.run() contains an infinite recursion when computing the counterfactual policy effectiveness. Several required metrics and CLI features are missing or misnamed.

issues.description: Simulation.run() computes a counterfactual by calling another Simulation.run(), which itself computes its own counterfactual, leading to infinite recursion.
issues.location: Simulation.run(), lines computing cf_sim and cf_res
issues.solution: Add a guard flag (e.g., self.p['_is_counterfactual']=True) to skip counterfactual computation for CF runs, or refactor to compute the CF result only once without nesting. Example: if self.p.get('_is_counterfactual'): skip computing policy_effectiveness_index.

issues.description: main() parses arguments but never constructs a Simulation instance, runs it, or outputs results. CLI flags (output, csv-out, validate, fast-smoke-run) are not honored.
issues.solution: After reading params and days, create and run the simulation: sim = Simulation(params, seed=args.seed); results = sim.run(days). Print JSON to stdout if no output file; write to args.output if provided; if args.csv_out, call sim.save_results; if args.validate set, call run_validations and print results; if args.fast_smoke_run, do a short run and print 'SMOKE_OK'.

issues.description: Policy effectiveness counterfactual uses the same run() logic that includes policy effectiveness computation again, even when mandate is already disabled. This magnifies the infinite recursion and is conceptually incorrect.
issues.solution: Compute the counterfactual adoption series once by running a CF simulation with a flag to disable further CF computations and then subtract from the baseline; do not nest CF inside CF.

issues.description: Required metrics are incomplete or misnamed relative to the task specification: missing final_adoption_rate, adoption_inequality_index (Gini), supply_shortage_days, enforcement_actions_count. Disease-layer metrics are not implemented or gated.
issues.solution: Add metrics: final_adoption_rate (last of adoption_rate), adoption_inequality_index using the provided gini() across demographic/identity groups, supply_shortage_days (count of days when demand > supply or inventory == 0), enforcement_actions_count (total incidents). If disease_model_enabled is false, set Rt_reduction and cumulative_infections to null or omit.

issues.description: adoption_inequality_index should use Gini (or Theil) as per spec; code computes variance across income quintiles and places it under inequality_in_adoption.
issues.solution: Replace inequality_in_adoption calculation with gini(quintile_rates) and expose as adoption_inequality_index.

issues.description: Validations rely on Simulation.run() and will also hit the infinite recursion (e.g., validate_replicate_consistency).
issues.solution: Fix the run() CF recursion first; optionally disable policy_effectiveness_index computation during validation runs via a flag in params.

issues.description: CLI feature 'fast-smoke-run' documented but not implemented.
issues.solution: If args.fast_smoke_run is true, run a tiny simulation (e.g., population_size=200, days=5) and print 'SMOKE_OK' without writing files.

issues.description: Many functions contain an initial 'pass' statement before the actual code. It's harmless but confusing.
issues.location: Multiple methods (e.g., clamp, gini, poisson_sample, Household.update_norm, etc.)
issues.solution: Remove redundant 'pass' statements from function bodies to improve readability.

issues.description: daily_new_adopters counts changes before enforcement-induced compliance is applied, potentially undercounting those who comply at entry later in the day.
issues.solution: Compute new adopters after enforcement interactions, or track pre-day vs end-of-day wearing state to capture all transitions.

issues.description: Some spec parameters are not used (e.g., enforcement_capacity_per_day, fine_amount alias only partially, rationing_policy 'first_come'), and several entity attributes/behaviors from the spec are not represented (e.g., fatigue_level, group_identity, health_status, daily_schedule).
issues.solution: Implement or at least wire in these parameters/attributes where feasible, or document they are currently unsupported. For enforcement_capacity, cap daily incidents; for rationing_policy, implement a first-come FIFO with unmet demand tracking.

issues.description: Due to the infinite recursion in run(), performance degrades catastrophically and the program will not complete.
issues.solution: Fix the counterfactual computation to avoid recursion as described earlier.
